title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Priya Nandakumar
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets have growing priority-routing traffic patterns where short bursts from high-priority customers cause transient head-of-line effects and noisy utilization metrics. This PR introduces a combined approach: (1) priority-aware burst tokenbucket controls that isolate short high-priority bursts without starving background tenants; (2) per-priority utilization reporting to give SRE and product teams accurate cost and SLO signals; and (3) a policy refactor to make priority routing + burst controls pluggable and observable.

Scope: single monorepo change touching autoscaler, routing, metrics collector, and the fleet reporting pipeline. All changes are behind the feature flag dedicated.autoscaler.priority_burst_v2 and default-off for existing customers.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced PriorityTokenBucket: a token-bucket variant that tracks tokens per-priority tier and enforces burst caps while allowing weighted background refill.
- Autoscaler integration: autoscaler now considers per-priority short-term headroom when computing scale-up decisions to avoid overscaling for low-latency priority spikes.
- Utilization reporting: metrics pipeline now emits redwood.dedicated.utilization.per_priority.{priority} for last-minute and 5m-window coverage; added sample_rate tagging and attribution to fleet and route.
- Policy refactor: split burst control logic out of scheduler into autoscaler/policy/priority_policy.go to enable unit tests and future variants (rate-limit, leaky-bucket).
- Console and dashboards: expose new heatmap and per-priority breakdown for fleet dashboards (UI PR forthcoming).

Backward compatibility: All runtime behavior is gated behind the feature flag and a new cluster config block. Existing autoscaler behavior remains unchanged unless the flag is enabled.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for PriorityTokenBucket edge cases (concurrent acquires, overflow, weighted refill) added.
- Integration tests simulate a mixed-priority workload (100k requests over 10s) and assert that high-priority latency stays <50ms while background throughput degrades gracefully.
- Load-run in perf-canary: 2 hourly runs against a 20-node dedicated cluster with the flag enabled; no regression observed in average latency or GPU utilization beyond expected smoothing.
- Metrics validation: added assertions that per-priority utilization metrics are emitted and attributed correctly in pipeline smoke tests.

Rollout plan: staged rollout to canary fleets -> small production fleets -> broad rollout. Feature flag controlled via admin console and infra config.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc updated (Linear ENG-1428).
- [x] Unit & integration tests.
- [x] Metrics & dashboards instrumentation.
- [x] Feature flag gated.
- [x] Perf canary runs green.

Notes: This PR is part of the broader Dedicated Autoscaler initiative for Q1 (see ENG-1499). Follow-up PRs will: (1) add a leaky-bucket policy variant, (2) expose per-priority cost breakouts in billing exports, and (3) UI changes in redwood-console.

release_notes: Added priority-aware burst tokenbucket to protect fleet stability during short high-priority spikes.
Per-priority utilization metrics (redwood.dedicated.utilization.per_priority.*) for better SLO and cost attribution.
Autoscaler now factors short-term per-priority headroom to reduce overscaling during bursts.
